newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi meets Spain's Aznar in Venice.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi meets Spain's Aznar in Venice.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi led his Spanish counterpart Jose Maria Aznar on a tour of Venice on Saturday in a meeting meant to improve recently strained ties between the two countries.

"I see the two countries sharing the same destiny," Prodi told reporters after meeting Aznar, who arrived in the northern lagoon city late on Friday for private talks with Prodi. He is due to return to Madrid on Sunday.
The prime ministers and their wives were due to spend the day together visiting the landmarks and museums of Venice.

Spain and Italy fell out last year after Prodi reportedly sought assurances from Aznar that he would support a joint bid to have the tough criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) relaxed.
Aznar refused and both have since redoubled their efforts to ensure that their economies are in shape for the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999.
The conservative Spanish leader said this week he was coming to Venice to improve relations with Italy.
"It's going very well," he told reporters on Saturday.
Prodi, head of Italy's centre-left government since last May, said it was time for the two countries to pass "from a stage of relations to a phase of continuous cooperation".
"We both have important tasks in the Mediterranean and last night we began to chat about things in a relaxed atmosphere," Prodi said.
